title: Gothic cathedral fragment - exercises every trap from the v4.14 field report
prompt:
Model a small Gothic cathedral fragment in Rhino, units mm. Build it in phases and use the rab helpers rather than raw rhinoscriptsyntax.

1. Layer tree, NESTED, with a deliberately repeated leaf name:
   Cath::01_Nave::Piers, Cath::01_Nave::Walls, Cath::02_Chevet::Piers, Cath::02_Chevet::Apse, Cath::03_Roof
2. Nave: two rows of 6 piers, 1500 x 1200 in plan, 14000 tall, rows 14500mm clear apart, bays at 8000mm centres, on Cath::01_Nave::Piers.
3. Nave walls: a wall on each side running the full length of the piers, 600 thick, 14000 tall, EACH with 4 pointed-arch window openings (2000 span, 1500 rise, sill at 6000). Put them on Cath::01_Nave::Walls. Note one wall runs along Y - use rab.wall_profile with a plane from rab.plane_from_wall so the openings actually cut.
4. Chevet: a semicircular apse wall (rab.annulus_wall) beyond the east end, inner radius 7000, outer 8000, 14000 tall, plus 5 radiating piers on Cath::02_Chevet::Piers.
5. Roof: a gable roof over the nave, eaves at 14000, ridge at 21000, on Cath::03_Roof.
6. Finally: assert the dimensions against the brief, check nothing floats, and capture an elevation set excluding nothing.

Work in phases, one heavy call per turn. Verify as you go.
notes: Traps this covers: nested layers with a duplicate leaf name (Piers appears twice) exercise the A1 count fix and the A2 by_layer descendant fix; the Y-running wall with openings exercises the A7 Extrusion.AddInnerProfile handedness workaround; annulus_wall exercises the apse primitive; watertight on the walls proves the boolean/orientation path; the dimension assertions exercise assert_dimensions.
